about: Authored query pairs on AdventureWorks for tools/sample_db_bench.py. label: 'equivalent' or 'different' under the declared keys minus 'drop' (not_null:T.c, pk:T, fk:T.c). A 'different' pair carries a witness: 'real' (the two queries already differ on the AdventureWorks data) or a small database (missing columns are completed with legal values) that satisfies the remaining declarations and separates them. 'sibling' names the pair it negates. BigQuery has no UNIQUE constraint, so the alternate keys upstream declares as unique indexes (Product.Name, Product.ProductNumber, every rowguid) are not declared keys and pairs that need them are 'different' under the declarations although the data agrees; SalesOrderDetailID alone is not a declared key either (the key is the pair with SalesOrderID).

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: SalesOrderDetail.SalesOrderID is NOT NULL and references SalesOrderHeader's key: every detail line joins exactly one header
pairs.left: SELECT d.SalesOrderID, d.SalesOrderDetailID, d.LineTotal FROM SalesOrderDetail AS d JOIN SalesOrderHeader AS h ON d.SalesOrderID = h.SalesOrderID
pairs.right: SELECT SalesOrderID, SalesOrderDetailID, LineTotal FROM SalesOrderDetail

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Customer.StoreID may be NULL (it is NULL for every individual customer, 18,484 of 19,820): such a customer joins no store
pairs.left: SELECT c.CustomerID, c.AccountNumber FROM Customer AS c JOIN Store AS s ON c.StoreID = s.BusinessEntityID
pairs.right: SELECT CustomerID, AccountNumber FROM Customer

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key a detail line may name a header that does not exist
pairs.left: SELECT d.SalesOrderID, d.SalesOrderDetailID, d.LineTotal FROM SalesOrderDetail AS d JOIN SalesOrderHeader AS h ON d.SalesOrderID = h.SalesOrderID
pairs.right: SELECT SalesOrderID, SalesOrderDetailID, LineTotal FROM SalesOrderDetail

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without SalesOrderHeader's primary key two headers may share an id and the join doubles the line
pairs.left: SELECT d.SalesOrderID, d.SalesOrderDetailID, d.LineTotal FROM SalesOrderDetail AS d JOIN SalesOrderHeader AS h ON d.SalesOrderID = h.SalesOrderID
pairs.right: SELECT SalesOrderID, SalesOrderDetailID, LineTotal FROM SalesOrderDetail

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: detail to header to customer, both foreign keys NOT NULL and onto primary keys: neither join changes the detail lines
pairs.left: SELECT d.SalesOrderID, d.SalesOrderDetailID, d.OrderQty FROM SalesOrderDetail AS d JOIN SalesOrderHeader AS h ON d.SalesOrderID = h.SalesOrderID JOIN Customer AS c ON h.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
pairs.right: SELECT SalesOrderID, SalesOrderDetailID, OrderQty FROM SalesOrderDetail

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without SalesOrderHeader.CustomerID's foreign key a header may name a customer that does not exist
pairs.left: SELECT d.SalesOrderID, d.SalesOrderDetailID, d.OrderQty FROM SalesOrderDetail AS d JOIN SalesOrderHeader AS h ON d.SalesOrderID = h.SalesOrderID JOIN Customer AS c ON h.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
pairs.right: SELECT SalesOrderID, SalesOrderDetailID, OrderQty FROM SalesOrderDetail

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the composite foreign key (SpecialOfferID, ProductID) is NOT NULL and onto SpecialOfferProduct's composite key
pairs.left: SELECT d.SalesOrderID, d.SalesOrderDetailID FROM SalesOrderDetail AS d JOIN SpecialOfferProduct AS sop ON d.SpecialOfferID = sop.SpecialOfferID AND d.ProductID = sop.ProductID
pairs.right: SELECT SalesOrderID, SalesOrderDetailID FROM SalesOrderDetail

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: joining on SpecialOfferID alone is not the foreign key: SpecialOfferProduct has many products per offer and the join repeats the line (shown on one order: unfiltered the repeated join has tens of millions of rows)
pairs.left: SELECT d.SalesOrderID, d.SalesOrderDetailID FROM SalesOrderDetail AS d JOIN SpecialOfferProduct AS sop ON d.SpecialOfferID = sop.SpecialOfferID WHERE d.SalesOrderID = 43659
pairs.right: SELECT SalesOrderID, SalesOrderDetailID FROM SalesOrderDetail WHERE SalesOrderID = 43659

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the composite foreign key a line may name an offer and product pair that does not exist
pairs.left: SELECT d.SalesOrderID, d.SalesOrderDetailID FROM SalesOrderDetail AS d JOIN SpecialOfferProduct AS sop ON d.SpecialOfferID = sop.SpecialOfferID AND d.ProductID = sop.ProductID
pairs.right: SELECT SalesOrderID, SalesOrderDetailID FROM SalesOrderDetail

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: an inner join on a nullable foreign key keeps exactly the rows whose foreign key is not NULL
pairs.left: SELECT c.CustomerID FROM Customer AS c JOIN Store AS s ON c.StoreID = s.BusinessEntityID
pairs.right: SELECT CustomerID FROM Customer WHERE StoreID IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key a customer may name a store that does not exist
pairs.left: SELECT c.CustomerID FROM Customer AS c JOIN Store AS s ON c.StoreID = s.BusinessEntityID
pairs.right: SELECT CustomerID FROM Customer WHERE StoreID IS NOT NULL

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a LEFT JOIN on the other table's primary key keeps each product once and none are lost; no column of ProductModel is read
pairs.left: SELECT p.ProductID, p.Name FROM Product AS p LEFT JOIN ProductModel AS pm ON p.ProductModelID = pm.ProductModelID
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID, Name FROM Product

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: SalesOrderDetail.ProductID is not a key: a product with several lines repeats, one without any is kept
pairs.left: SELECT p.ProductID, p.Name FROM Product AS p LEFT JOIN SalesOrderDetail AS d ON d.ProductID = p.ProductID
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID, Name FROM Product

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without ProductModel's primary key two models may share an id and the product repeats
pairs.left: SELECT p.ProductID, p.Name FROM Product AS p LEFT JOIN ProductModel AS pm ON p.ProductModelID = pm.ProductModelID
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID, Name FROM Product

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: BusinessEntityAddress.AddressID is NOT NULL and references Address's key
pairs.left: SELECT bea.BusinessEntityID, bea.AddressTypeID FROM BusinessEntityAddress AS bea JOIN Address AS a ON bea.AddressID = a.AddressID
pairs.right: SELECT BusinessEntityID, AddressTypeID FROM BusinessEntityAddress

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the foreign key a row may name an address that does not exist
pairs.left: SELECT bea.BusinessEntityID, bea.AddressTypeID FROM BusinessEntityAddress AS bea JOIN Address AS a ON bea.AddressID = a.AddressID
pairs.right: SELECT BusinessEntityID, AddressTypeID FROM BusinessEntityAddress

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: Person's primary key is also a NOT NULL foreign key onto BusinessEntity's: each person has exactly one business entity
pairs.left: SELECT p.BusinessEntityID, p.LastName FROM Person AS p JOIN BusinessEntity AS be ON p.BusinessEntityID = be.BusinessEntityID
pairs.right: SELECT BusinessEntityID, LastName FROM Person

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: BusinessEntity has rows that are not people (vendors and stores): read from that side the join drops them
pairs.left: SELECT be.BusinessEntityID FROM BusinessEntity AS be JOIN Person AS p ON p.BusinessEntityID = be.BusinessEntityID
pairs.right: SELECT BusinessEntityID FROM BusinessEntity

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a self join on the primary key matches each row with itself
pairs.left: SELECT a.ProductID, a.Name FROM Product AS a JOIN Product AS b ON a.ProductID = b.ProductID
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID, Name FROM Product

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the primary key two products may share an id and the self join pairs each with both
pairs.left: SELECT a.ProductID, a.Name FROM Product AS a JOIN Product AS b ON a.ProductID = b.ProductID
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID, Name FROM Product

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Product.Name is unique upstream (a unique index) but BigQuery has no UNIQUE constraint, so it is not a declared key: two products may share a name
pairs.left: SELECT a.ProductID FROM Product AS a JOIN Product AS b ON a.Name = b.Name
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID FROM Product

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: ProductID is the primary key, so the rows are already distinct
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT ProductID, Name FROM Product
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID, Name FROM Product

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the primary key two products may be the same row
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT ProductID, Name FROM Product
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID, Name FROM Product

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Color is not a key: many products share a colour
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT Color FROM Product
pairs.right: SELECT Color FROM Product

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Product.ProductNumber is unique upstream (a unique index) but not a declared key: two products may share a number
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT ProductNumber FROM Product
pairs.right: SELECT ProductNumber FROM Product

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: (SalesOrderID, SalesOrderDetailID) is the composite primary key
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT SalesOrderID, SalesOrderDetailID, ProductID FROM SalesOrderDetail
pairs.right: SELECT SalesOrderID, SalesOrderDetailID, ProductID FROM SalesOrderDetail

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: SalesOrderID alone is part of the key: an order has many lines
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT SalesOrderID FROM SalesOrderDetail
pairs.right: SELECT SalesOrderID FROM SalesOrderDetail

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: SalesOrderDetailID alone is not the key, only the pair is (the column is unique in the data, an identity, but no unique constraint is declared): two lines of different orders may share it
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT SalesOrderDetailID FROM SalesOrderDetail
pairs.right: SELECT SalesOrderDetailID FROM SalesOrderDetail

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the join is onto ProductSubcategory's key (at most one match per product) and ProductID is Product's key
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT p.ProductID, p.Name FROM Product AS p JOIN ProductSubcategory AS ps ON p.ProductSubcategoryID = ps.ProductSubcategoryID
pairs.right: SELECT p.ProductID, p.Name FROM Product AS p JOIN ProductSubcategory AS ps ON p.ProductSubcategoryID = ps.ProductSubcategoryID

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: joined to SalesOrderDetail, which has many lines per product, the same product repeats and DISTINCT on it matters
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT p.ProductID FROM Product AS p JOIN SalesOrderDetail AS d ON d.ProductID = p.ProductID
pairs.right: SELECT p.ProductID FROM Product AS p JOIN SalesOrderDetail AS d ON d.ProductID = p.ProductID

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the four columns are EmployeeDepartmentHistory's primary key (it includes a DATE column)
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT BusinessEntityID, StartDate, DepartmentID, ShiftID FROM EmployeeDepartmentHistory
pairs.right: SELECT BusinessEntityID, StartDate, DepartmentID, ShiftID FROM EmployeeDepartmentHistory

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: BusinessEntityID and DepartmentID are two of the four key columns: an employee may return to a department on a later date
pairs.left: SELECT DISTINCT BusinessEntityID, DepartmentID FROM EmployeeDepartmentHistory
pairs.right: SELECT BusinessEntityID, DepartmentID FROM EmployeeDepartmentHistory

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: SalesOrderHeader.CustomerID is NOT NULL: COUNT of it counts every row
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(CustomerID) FROM SalesOrderHeader
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SalesOrderHeader

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Customer.StoreID is NULL for individual customers
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(StoreID) FROM Customer
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Customer

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: ListPrice is a function of the primary key ProductID, already in the group
pairs.left: SELECT p.ProductID, p.Name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Product AS p JOIN SalesOrderDetail AS d ON d.ProductID = p.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.Name, p.ListPrice
pairs.right: SELECT p.ProductID, p.Name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Product AS p JOIN SalesOrderDetail AS d ON d.ProductID = p.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.Name

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: SalesOrderDetail.SpecialOfferID is not a function of ProductID: a product sells under several offers
pairs.left: SELECT ProductID, COUNT(*) AS n FROM SalesOrderDetail GROUP BY ProductID, SpecialOfferID
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID, COUNT(*) AS n FROM SalesOrderDetail GROUP BY ProductID

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the primary key two products may share an id and differ in ListPrice: the groups differ
pairs.left: SELECT p.ProductID, p.Name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Product AS p JOIN SalesOrderDetail AS d ON d.ProductID = p.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.Name, p.ListPrice
pairs.right: SELECT p.ProductID, p.Name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Product AS p JOIN SalesOrderDetail AS d ON d.ProductID = p.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.Name

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: SalesOrderID is the primary key of SalesOrderHeader
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT SalesOrderID) FROM SalesOrderHeader
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SalesOrderHeader

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: CustomerID repeats: a customer places many orders
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CustomerID) FROM SalesOrderHeader
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SalesOrderHeader

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: SalesOrderDetailID alone is not the key (only the pair with SalesOrderID is)
pairs.left: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT SalesOrderDetailID) FROM SalesOrderDetail
pairs.right: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SalesOrderDetail

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a HAVING on a grouping column is a WHERE before the grouping
pairs.left: SELECT ProductID, SUM(OrderQty) AS q FROM SalesOrderDetail GROUP BY ProductID HAVING ProductID < 800
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID, SUM(OrderQty) AS q FROM SalesOrderDetail WHERE ProductID < 800 GROUP BY ProductID

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a HAVING on the sum is not a WHERE on the rows
pairs.left: SELECT ProductID, SUM(OrderQty) AS q FROM SalesOrderDetail GROUP BY ProductID HAVING SUM(OrderQty) > 100
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID, SUM(OrderQty) AS q FROM SalesOrderDetail WHERE OrderQty > 100 GROUP BY ProductID

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a filter on the grouping column commutes with the grouping
pairs.left: SELECT * FROM (SELECT CustomerID, COUNT(*) AS n FROM SalesOrderHeader GROUP BY CustomerID) WHERE CustomerID = 11000
pairs.right: SELECT CustomerID, COUNT(*) AS n FROM SalesOrderHeader WHERE CustomerID = 11000 GROUP BY CustomerID

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: Customer's primary key makes one group per customer, and the count of the joined orders is the count of the subquery
pairs.left: SELECT c.CustomerID, COUNT(h.SalesOrderID) AS orders FROM Customer AS c LEFT JOIN SalesOrderHeader AS h ON h.CustomerID = c.CustomerID GROUP BY c.CustomerID
pairs.right: SELECT c.CustomerID, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SalesOrderHeader AS h WHERE h.CustomerID = c.CustomerID) AS orders FROM Customer AS c

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the primary key two customers may share an id and the group merges them
pairs.left: SELECT c.CustomerID, COUNT(h.SalesOrderID) AS orders FROM Customer AS c LEFT JOIN SalesOrderHeader AS h ON h.CustomerID = c.CustomerID GROUP BY c.CustomerID
pairs.right: SELECT c.CustomerID, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SalesOrderHeader AS h WHERE h.CustomerID = c.CustomerID) AS orders FROM Customer AS c

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: IN on a not null column is a correlated EXISTS
pairs.left: SELECT ProductID FROM Product WHERE ProductID IN (SELECT ProductID FROM SalesOrderDetail WHERE OrderQty > 20)
pairs.right: SELECT p.ProductID FROM Product AS p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM SalesOrderDetail AS d WHERE d.ProductID = p.ProductID AND d.OrderQty > 20)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a join repeats a product once per matching line, IN does not
pairs.left: SELECT ProductID FROM Product WHERE ProductID IN (SELECT ProductID FROM SalesOrderDetail WHERE OrderQty > 20)
pairs.right: SELECT p.ProductID FROM Product AS p JOIN SalesOrderDetail AS d ON d.ProductID = p.ProductID WHERE d.OrderQty > 20

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: TerritoryID is SalesTerritory's primary key: the join matches at most one row, as IN does
pairs.left: SELECT CustomerID FROM Customer WHERE TerritoryID IN (SELECT TerritoryID FROM SalesTerritory WHERE `Group` = 'Europe')
pairs.right: SELECT c.CustomerID FROM Customer AS c JOIN SalesTerritory AS t ON c.TerritoryID = t.TerritoryID WHERE t.`Group` = 'Europe'

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without the primary key two territories may share an id and the join repeats the customer
pairs.left: SELECT CustomerID FROM Customer WHERE TerritoryID IN (SELECT TerritoryID FROM SalesTerritory WHERE `Group` = 'Europe')
pairs.right: SELECT c.CustomerID FROM Customer AS c JOIN SalesTerritory AS t ON c.TerritoryID = t.TerritoryID WHERE t.`Group` = 'Europe'

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: BillOfMaterials.ComponentID is NOT NULL: NOT IN and NOT EXISTS agree
pairs.left: SELECT ProductID FROM Product WHERE ProductID NOT IN (SELECT ComponentID FROM BillOfMaterials)
pairs.right: SELECT p.ProductID FROM Product AS p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM BillOfMaterials AS b WHERE b.ComponentID = p.ProductID)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: BillOfMaterials.ProductAssemblyID is NULL for raw materials (25 rows): NOT IN over it returns no row at all
pairs.left: SELECT ProductID FROM Product WHERE ProductID NOT IN (SELECT ProductAssemblyID FROM BillOfMaterials)
pairs.right: SELECT p.ProductID FROM Product AS p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM BillOfMaterials AS b WHERE b.ProductAssemblyID = p.ProductID)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: without NOT NULL on ComponentID a NULL component makes NOT IN return nothing
pairs.left: SELECT ProductID FROM Product WHERE ProductID NOT IN (SELECT ComponentID FROM BillOfMaterials)
pairs.right: SELECT p.ProductID FROM Product AS p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM BillOfMaterials AS b WHERE b.ComponentID = p.ProductID)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: Product.Name is NOT NULL
pairs.left: SELECT ProductID FROM Product WHERE Name IS NULL
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID FROM Product WHERE FALSE

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Product.Color is nullable
pairs.left: SELECT ProductID FROM Product WHERE Color IS NULL
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID FROM Product WHERE FALSE

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: Product.Name is NOT NULL, so COALESCE returns it
pairs.left: SELECT ProductID, COALESCE(Name, 'x') AS Name FROM Product
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID, Name FROM Product

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Product.Color is nullable
pairs.left: SELECT ProductID, COALESCE(Color, 'x') AS Color FROM Product
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID, Color FROM Product

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: NOT (a = b) is a <> b for NOT NULL columns
pairs.left: SELECT ProductID FROM Product WHERE NOT (SafetyStockLevel = ReorderPoint)
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID FROM Product WHERE SafetyStockLevel <> ReorderPoint

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: Product.Weight is nullable: for a NULL weight NOT (Weight = 5) is NULL and the row is dropped, while Weight <> 5 OR Weight IS NULL keeps it
pairs.left: SELECT ProductID FROM Product WHERE NOT (Weight = 5)
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID FROM Product WHERE Weight <> 5 OR Weight IS NULL

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: UNION DISTINCT removes duplicates across and within the inputs
pairs.left: SELECT CustomerID FROM SalesOrderHeader UNION ALL SELECT CustomerID FROM Customer
pairs.right: SELECT CustomerID FROM SalesOrderHeader UNION DISTINCT SELECT CustomerID FROM Customer

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the two filters on a NOT NULL column partition the table
pairs.left: SELECT SalesOrderID FROM SalesOrderHeader WHERE Status > 4 UNION ALL SELECT SalesOrderID FROM SalesOrderHeader WHERE Status <= 4
pairs.right: SELECT SalesOrderID FROM SalesOrderHeader

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: on a nullable column a NULL row is in neither filter
pairs.left: SELECT ProductID FROM Product WHERE Weight > 5 UNION ALL SELECT ProductID FROM Product WHERE Weight <= 5
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID FROM Product

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: INTERSECT DISTINCT on NOT NULL columns is DISTINCT with IN
pairs.left: SELECT CustomerID FROM SalesOrderHeader INTERSECT DISTINCT SELECT CustomerID FROM Customer
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT h.CustomerID FROM SalesOrderHeader AS h WHERE h.CustomerID IN (SELECT CustomerID FROM Customer)

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: INTERSECT treats two NULLs as equal, IN does not match them
pairs.left: SELECT StoreID FROM Customer INTERSECT DISTINCT SELECT SalesPersonID FROM Store
pairs.right: SELECT DISTINCT c.StoreID FROM Customer AS c WHERE c.StoreID IN (SELECT SalesPersonID FROM Store)

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: the WHERE on the right side's column rejects the NULL-extended rows, so the LEFT JOIN is an inner join
pairs.left: SELECT h.SalesOrderID, d.OrderQty FROM SalesOrderHeader AS h LEFT JOIN SalesOrderDetail AS d ON d.SalesOrderID = h.SalesOrderID WHERE d.OrderQty > 5
pairs.right: SELECT h.SalesOrderID, d.OrderQty FROM SalesOrderHeader AS h JOIN SalesOrderDetail AS d ON d.SalesOrderID = h.SalesOrderID WHERE d.OrderQty > 5

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: the filter accepts NULL, so the NULL-extended rows survive the LEFT JOIN
pairs.left: SELECT h.SalesOrderID, d.OrderQty FROM SalesOrderHeader AS h LEFT JOIN SalesOrderDetail AS d ON d.SalesOrderID = h.SalesOrderID AND d.OrderQty > 100 WHERE d.OrderQty > 100 OR d.OrderQty IS NULL
pairs.right: SELECT h.SalesOrderID, d.OrderQty FROM SalesOrderHeader AS h JOIN SalesOrderDetail AS d ON d.SalesOrderID = h.SalesOrderID AND d.OrderQty > 100 WHERE d.OrderQty > 100 OR d.OrderQty IS NULL

pairs.label: equivalent
pairs.why: a filter on the partition column removes whole partitions: the ranks of the rest do not change
pairs.left: SELECT ProductID, SalesOrderID, r FROM (SELECT ProductID, SalesOrderID, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY ProductID ORDER BY OrderQty) AS r FROM SalesOrderDetail) WHERE ProductID = 776
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID, SalesOrderID, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY ProductID ORDER BY OrderQty) AS r FROM SalesOrderDetail WHERE ProductID = 776

pairs.label: different
pairs.why: a filter on another column removes rows from inside the partitions and the ranks change
pairs.left: SELECT ProductID, SalesOrderID, r FROM (SELECT ProductID, SalesOrderID, OrderQty, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY ProductID ORDER BY OrderQty) AS r FROM SalesOrderDetail) WHERE OrderQty > 3
pairs.right: SELECT ProductID, SalesOrderID, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY ProductID ORDER BY OrderQty) AS r FROM SalesOrderDetail WHERE OrderQty > 3
